newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian leader signs political pact into law.
newsitem.headline: Algerian leader signs political pact into law.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Tuesday ordered a pact reached with politicians at the weekend to be published in the official gazette, effectively making it the law of the land.

Zeroual's order, reported by the official news agency APS, means that the pact, which bars the use of religion or language as a basis for political parties, will govern general elections promised for 1997.
The pact also sets a framework for a multi-party democracy and condemns violence which the authorities have blamed on Moslem militants.

Most of the politicians who signed the agreement at a National Conference of Understanding are, however, seen largely as lacking popular support. The two main secular parties boycotted the meeting while the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was banned because of its outlaw status.
The FIS dominated the country's last general election, cancelled in January 1992. Since then, an estimated 50,000 people have been killed.
Justice Minister Mohamed Adami affixed the official seals to the pact shortly after it was signed at the National Conference.
